instances.title: Broken paired signs
instances.why_summary: This example begins with the sparse holdout chain, with coefficients \(1/2\), and adds \[ \frac13\cdot X_0^2\cdot X_1\cdot X_2\cdot Y_0\cdot Y_2. \] The target remains \(X_0^3\cdot Y_0^3\), and every mixed term still has \(X/Y\)-bidegree \((4,2)\). The added term breaks the separate paired sign changes in the first two pairs, while preserving their product and the third paired sign change. It is a controlled loss of symmetry rather than a generic dense perturbation.

instances.title: Dense rational · full coefficient support
instances.why_summary: This is a deliberately contrasting test beside the sparse, highly organized examples. The sextic contains all 236 monomials of total degree six that are even under the global \(Y\)-sign involution. The six pure sixth powers have coefficient one; every other coefficient is a small, explicitly specified rational number with denominator \(9973\). The target remains the short monomial \(X_0^3\cdot Y_0^3\).

instances.title: Cyclic coupling · pole order two
instances.why_summary: Use the cyclic three-link sextic from [the degree-six cyclic instance](#case/cycle-three), with \[ q=2,\qquad A=X_0^2\cdot X_1^2\cdot X_2^3\cdot Y_0^2\cdot Y_1^2\cdot Y_2. \] Every coordinate occurs, and the unequal exponents in the final pair distinguish one position in the cycle. Cyclic permutation produces two companion targets on the same hypersurface. A construction for their invariant sum must still separate the other components to serve the specified target.

instances.title: Quadric contact · residual sector
instances.why_summary: The [broken-reflection construction](#case/quadric-contact-broken) reduces this sextic to a cubic surface using the quadratic coordinates \(S=2(X_0^2+Y_0^2)\), \(T=4X_0Y_0\), and passive ratios. Its Jacobian supplies the factor \(X_0^2-Y_0^2\), which changes sign under \(X_0\leftrightarrow Y_0\). The target served there has precisely that sign. Here the variety is unchanged, but \(A=X_0^3\cdot Y_0^3\) is invariant under the same exchange. It therefore cannot be obtained as a polynomial density through that particular quotient map. The other visible exchange, \(X_1\leftrightarrow Y_1\), also fixes this target. This isolates a question about which cohomology classes the construction reaches, rather than about finding lines on another cubic surface. A certificate would need a different transfer, a support serving the complementary sector, or a way to combine constructions beyond these quotient densities; the stated obstruction does not exclude such possibilities.

instances.title: One reflection · skew coupling
instances.why_summary: The sextic of [One reflection · residual sector](#case/one-reflection) has hidden exchanges of \(Y_0\) and \(Y_1\), which allow its target to split between two cubic-surface constructions. The additional term \[ \frac17\cdot X_0\cdot X_1\cdot Y_0\cdot Y_1\cdot(Y_0^2-Y_1^2) \] breaks those exchanges while preserving the prescribed involution and the separate \(Y_2\) reflection. The target \(X_0^3\cdot Y_0^3\) is even in \(Y_2\), so that surviving reflection does not serve it. Smoothness follows from a direct derivative estimate: the mixed terms cannot cancel the pure sixth-power derivative at a coordinate of maximal modulus.

instances.title: Reflection · complementary character
instances.why_summary: The [coupled Fano construction](#case/reflection-coupled-fano) supplies an explicit weighted quartic, a nonsingular deformation system, and a polynomial primitive on the quotient by \(Y_2\mapsto-Y_2\). Here the sextic is unchanged, but the target is \(A=X_0^3\cdot Y_0^3\), which is even in \(Y_2\). The example tests the target boundary of a successful construction on exactly the same geometry.

instances.title: Cyclic triple cover · complementary character
instances.why_summary: The [cyclic triple-cover density target](#case/cyclic-triple-fano) uses \(Z=X_2^3\) to reach a weighted Fano quotient. Its explicit free line and nonsingular six-variable incidence provide polynomial primitives on that quotient. This companion retains the exact same sextic and changes only the source to \(A=X_0^3\cdot Y_0^3\). It asks what can be done outside the cubic density sector.

instances.title: Simultaneous permutations · standard sector
instances.why_summary: The sextic is invariant under simultaneous permutations of the three \(X/Y\) pairs. A transposition exchanges two \(X\) coordinates and two \(Y\) coordinates at once. Its fixed subspace has codimension two, so it is not a reflection. The equation couples all three pairs and has scalar Hessian symmetrizer, ruling out a linear block decomposition.
